stem: An infant with suspected non-IgE-mediated food allergy is breastfed and the mother is advised to eliminate cow milk and soy; what additional counselling should be given?

options.text: Use allergy testing instead of elimination

explanation: Calcium supplements should be suggested. When a breastfeeding mother eliminates cow milk and soy, she should also be advised about calcium supplementation to reduce nutritional deficiency risk.

citations.source: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf
citations.title: Louisa Leone MD3 2025 - Child and Adolescent Health - Study Notes.pdf

rationale: Maternal elimination can be part of management in a breastfed infant with suspected non-IgE-mediated food allergy, and cow milk plus soy avoidance in the mother should trigger advice on calcium supplementation.

optionExplanations.A: Correct because eliminating cow milk and soy can reduce dietary calcium intake, so supplementation should be advised
optionExplanations.B: Incorrect because skin prick testing is not the key counselling point for a suspected non-IgE-mediated food allergy managed by elimination
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because improvement may take time and is not expected immediately after the first feed change
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because management is based on clinical elimination rather than substituting routine allergy testing
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because breastfeeding can continue and maternal elimination is a recognised management approach
